name: Salesforce Connected App Per Org
description: Salesforce Connected App Per Org describes a customer-managed OAuth client configured inside one Salesforce organization with its own callback, scopes, user-access policy and token controls.
agentUseSummary: This legacy per-organization OAuth setup is visible as a canonical Salesforce extension preview. Relay will not collect an org's consumer secret or create parallel Salesforce sessions and tools beside the packaged canonical connector.

capabilities.label: Use organization-managed Salesforce OAuth
capabilities.description: If customer-managed identity is approved, extend the canonical Salesforce connector with an immutable organization, instance, client, callback, scope and token-policy binding.

blocked.label: Create duplicate Salesforce provider state
blocked.description: A per-org app listing must not create a parallel session, token, tool or approval surface beside Relay's canonical Salesforce connector.

blocked.label: Capture Salesforce consumer credentials
blocked.description: Relay will not ask an org administrator to paste a consumer secret, certificate private key or other connected-app credential into this Marketplace alias.

blocked.label: Create or administer a Salesforce app
blocked.description: Creating, installing, rotating, assigning or deleting Connected Apps and External Client Apps is Salesforce organization administration outside Relay agent actions.

blocked.label: Relax OAuth access controls
blocked.description: Relay will not broaden scopes, permit every user, relax IP restrictions or weaken refresh-token and session policies for an org-managed app.

blocked.label: Run Salesforce actions from the setup alias
blocked.description: This alias exposes no runtime actions; approved per-org identity must reuse the canonical connector's exact organization binding, typed reads, approvals and audits.

approvalProfiles.label: Salesforce organization OAuth security review
approvalProfiles.description: This setup alias is not connectable. Per-org credentials remain unavailable unless the canonical Salesforce connector has a least-privilege, revocable customer-managed identity design.

runtimeSupport.description: This alias installs no OpenClaw tools; organization-managed identity must extend the canonical Salesforce provider pack.
This alias installs no Hermes tools; organization-managed identity must extend the canonical Salesforce provider pack.

providerSetup.blocker: Salesforce Connected Apps define org-specific OAuth identity, scopes, permitted users, IP restrictions, refresh-token policy and sessions. New Connected App creation is restricted as of Spring '26 and Salesforce recommends External Client Apps. Relay already uses a packaged External Client App on the canonical connector and does not support customer-owned Salesforce credentials.
providerSetup.nextAction: Prefer the Relay-owned packaged External Client App on the canonical Salesforce connector. For an approved customer-managed case, extend that connector with immutable client, organization and instance binding, exact callbacks and scopes, PKCE, admin-approved users, IP controls, refresh-token rotation and expiry, revocation, credential rotation, and the existing typed read policies.

evidence.supports: Salesforce describes Connected Apps as API and identity integrations with policies controlling data access and expiry, notes new creation is restricted from Spring '26, and recommends External Client Apps.
Salesforce documents administrator-controlled permitted users, profile or permission-set assignment, IP restrictions, refresh-token lifetime and revocation policies for Connected Apps.
Salesforce documents OAuth scopes and refresh-token rotation, including invalidating used tokens and associated sessions on detected replay.
Salesforce states scopes bound the resources an OAuth client can access, tokens are issued per connected-app and user combination, and distinct service providers should use distinct apps.
